title: Ka-abag o Babag? Exploring the Lived Experiences in the Context of Financial Well-being of Microfinance Borrowers
authors: Estorba, V. L.; Relativo, J. L. C.; Rellon, S. B. S.; Regis, K. J. M.
venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science (IJRISS)
tldr: Microfinance acts as both support (ka-abag) and hindrance (babag) for Filipino borrowers, providing short-term relief while potentially perpetuating stress and debt dependency.
problem_and_motivation: Previous research on microfinance borrowers' financial well-being focuses heavily on quantitative measures without capturing lived experiences and coping strategies.
approach: Qualitative transcendental phenomenological design with 15 purposively selected female borrowers from Argao, Cebu.
Inclusion criteria: at least three years borrowing experience and multiple active loans.
In-depth interviews analyzed using Colaizzi's (1978) method.
Guided by Lazarus and Folkman's Transactional Model of Stress and Coping and Sen's Capability Approach.
findings: Nine major themes emerged including Living on the Edge of Survival, Debt Burden and Psychological Strain, Adaptive Financial Management.
Microfinance provides short-term relief and promotes financial discipline.
Microfinance can also perpetuate stress and debt dependency.
Effective coping strategies enable borrowers to navigate poverty more intentionally.
Microfinance has a dual nature as both ka-abag (support) and babag (hindrance).

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides rich qualitative evidence of the dual nature of microfinance for Filipino borrowers. Reveals how microfinance simultaneously supports and hinders financial well-being. Documents coping strategies and psychological dimensions of debt.
directly_justifies: Microfinance provides short-term relief but can perpetuate debt dependency.
Effective coping strategies enable borrowers to navigate poverty more intentionally.
Microfinance has a dual nature as both support and hindrance.
limits: Qualitative design with 15 participants limits generalizability.
Single location in Argao, Cebu limits geographic scope.
